\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We present the first controlled comparison showing that the structural pruning criterion substantially shapes post-RLVR recovery capacity.
Under identical GRPO training at 20\% sparsity, CKA-only pruning enables active learning (peak reward 0.354, 4.4$\times$ Standard), while importance-based methods collapse. Extended training to 300 steps confirms this gap is structural, not a matter of training budget.

The mechanism is preserved representational diversity: CKA-only diverges most from the dense representation ($\mu{=}0.62$ diagonal CKA) yet recovers best, while collapsing methods preserve dense fidelity ($\mu{\geq}0.88$).
Gradient importance removes structures that are representationally unique, destroying the exploration capacity that RL requires.
Cross-scale experiments on 1.5B confirm the same ordering, with the CKA-only advantage widening from 5.5\,pp to 13.2\,pp at smaller scale.
Reward-accuracy decoupling on GSM8K and MATH-500 further confirms that recovery capacity, not reward, is the appropriate diagnostic for pruned model quality.
Future work should validate the gradient across model families and RL algorithms beyond GRPO.
